title: Sum of Nodes with Even-Valued Grandparent
summary: Calculate the total sum of node values where the grandparent node has an even value.
statement: Calculate the total sum of node values where the grandparent node has an even value. If no such nodes exist, return 0. A grandparent is defined as the parent of a node's parent.
constraints: root is a nonempty binary tree.
A node qualifies when its grandparent exists and has an even value.
Return the sum of all qualifying node values.

At each node, add its value only when the remembered grandparent is even.
Recurse to children with current value becoming parent and old parent becoming grandparent.
Each node is visited with exactly its two ancestors, so the predicate is evaluated once and correctly.
editorial: A depth-first traversal carries the previous two ancestor values. The current node contributes precisely when the older value exists and is even. Passing values rather than searching upward keeps every visit constant-time. The oracle independently reconstructs the serialized tree and performs breadth-first traversal with explicit ancestor tuples.
